wake.title: Wake word
wake.nameText: What do you want to say to call K-Desktop? It learns from your voice, so it can be a made-up word such as “KDesktop”.
wake.nameTips: Best with 2 to 4 syllables and not something you say in normal conversation. You can add several, each with its own recording.
wake.silenceText: Stay quiet for 3 seconds so I can measure the background noise where you are.
wake.noise.medium: Medium background noise ({0}). Should be fine.
wake.noise.high: Quite a lot of background noise ({0}): the word will be recognised less well. If you can, turn the music off or move the mic away from the fan.
wake.wordText: Say “{0}” in your normal voice, the way you would to call K-Desktop. I’ll record it {1} times in a row (at least {2} are needed): wait for the meter to move and say it.
wake.issue.NoSpeech: I didn’t hear you. Press to continue and say it again.
wake.issue.TooShort: Too short. Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.issue.TooLong: Too long (over 2.5 s). Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.issue.TooQuiet: Very quiet: move closer to the mic or speak louder.
wake.issue.Clipped: Clipped: move a little away from the mic or lower its volume.
wake.issue.Odd: Very different from the others. Press to continue and repeat it.
wake.speechText: Now talk normally for about 10 seconds WITHOUT saying the word: read the text below or tell what you did today. This way your normal speech won’t set it off by mistake.
wake.speechSample: “This morning I checked my email, tidied a few folders on the desktop and then put on some music while I was cooking.”
wake.speechNone: I didn’t hear you speak. You can repeat it, or go on with the default threshold ({0}).
wake.speechDone: Done: the closest thing you said reached {0}; the threshold is {1}.
wake.testText: Say “{0}” (and, if you like, an order after it: “{0}, open the browser”) to see whether it is recognised. Try as many times as you like.

voice.downloadError: The voice models could not be downloaded: {0}
event.summary.idle: After {0} min without using the PC
event.summary.session.Suspend: When the PC goes to sleep
event.loopStopped: The event “{0}” fires too many times in a row: it stops for {1} min
history.hint: The last 500 runs, newest first: from where, how long they took and how they went. Double-click opens the command.
event.enabledHint: On: K-Desktop watches for what sets it off
event.emptyText: An event runs commands on its own when something happens: a program opens, a time of day, a while without using the PC, locking it…
event.suspended: Stopped for a few minutes: it fired too many times in a row (a loop?)
event.testHint: Runs its commands now, without checking «Only if» or the pause
event.noCommands: It doesn't run anything yet: add one or more commands (they run in this order; drag to change it).
event.exitNote: On exit they all run at once, 5 s at most, so exiting never hangs.
event.endHint.ProcessStart: When the program closes (with several windows or processes, when the last one closes).
event.endHint.Foreground: When it stops being in front.
event.endHint.Idle: When you use the PC again.
event.endHint.AudioDevice: When it is disconnected, or stops being the default output.
event.endHint.Network: When it disconnects from that network (or there is network again).
event.conditionsHint: If they aren't met it doesn't run (the log says why). Leave empty what you don't want to use.
event.cooldownHint: If it fires again sooner, it does nothing. 0 = always. Also, an event that fires more than 10 times in a minute stops for 10 minutes.
event.deleteText: Delete “{0}”? Its commands are not deleted.
event.runIfMissed: If it was missed, run it on start
event.runIfMissedHint: If K-Desktop was closed or the PC asleep at that time, it runs as soon as it can (once, the last one missed).
event.includeRunning: Also if it was already open when K-Desktop started
event.hint.appStart: Runs every time K-Desktop starts, its commands one after another and the events in the order of the list (drag to change it). Not after an update, nor while paused.
event.hint.appExit: Runs when K-Desktop exits, when the Windows session ends or when shutting down with the Power action. Not when it restarts to update itself.
event.hint.interval: It counts from when K-Desktop starts (or from when you change the event).
event.hint.processStart: Checked every 2 seconds. With several programs, it starts when the first opens and ends when the last closes.
event.hint.foreground: When one of these programs comes to the front (with a short margin so a quick Alt+Tab doesn't count).
event.hint.idle: No keyboard or mouse in that time. What macros, K-Board or the web app touchpad type or move also counts as using the PC.
event.hint.session: When going to sleep Windows leaves very little time: use quick commands (mute, pause the music…).
enum.session.Suspend: When the PC goes to sleep
event.kind.AppStart.desc: What used to be «Run on startup» in each command.
event.kind.AppExit.desc: What used to be «Run on exit» in each command.
event.kind.Time.desc: Every day or only on some days of the week, at the time you say.
event.kind.Interval.desc: Every N minutes while K-Desktop is running.
event.kind.ProcessStart.desc: When it opens (and, in «When it ends», when it closes). For example: when Steam opens, audio output to the headphones.
event.kind.Foreground.desc: When its window comes to the front (and, in «When it ends», when it stops being there).
event.kind.Idle.desc: After some minutes without touching the keyboard or mouse (and, in «When it ends», when you come back).
event.kind.Session.desc: When the session is locked or unlocked, or the PC goes to sleep or wakes up.
event.kind.PowerSource.desc: When a laptop goes on battery or back on mains power.
event.kind.File.desc: When a file appears (created, copied, downloaded…), as soon as it stops growing. For example, a new image in the ComfyUI output folder.
event.kind.RemoteCall.desc: When another computer, Home Assistant or a script asks for it by name, over UDP or the web.
event.summary.remoteCallOwn: When a call with its name arrives
event.hint.remoteCall: Case and accents don’t matter. Over UDP it needs «Remote control» on (and «Allow from other computers» if it isn’t this PC); over the web, another computer needs the token of a paired device.
event.hint.remoteCallExamples:
UDP:  event puerta
HTTP: POST http://<PC>:2502/api/event
      X-KD: 1
      Authorization: Bearer <token>
      {"name": "puerta"}
event.kind.Device.desc: When a USB stick, disk or card is connected (and, in «When it ends», when it is removed).
event.kind.Network.desc: When connecting to a network (or any) or when left without network; «When it ends», when that changes back.
event.kind.Gadget.desc: When a controller (Bluetooth or USB), a keyboard, a headset, a USB gadget… is connected; «When it ends», when it is disconnected. For example: when the controller is turned on, open Steam Big Picture.
event.endHint.Gadget: When it is disconnected (with a name, when the last thing with that name goes).
event.endHint.Load: When it stops holding for the same time (back to normal).
event.hint.gadget: Names are the Device Manager’s; the list includes paired Bluetooth devices even when they are off. Part of the name is enough («8bitdo», «xbox»). A Bluetooth device counts only while connected; it may take up to 15 s to be noticed.
event.kind.Load.desc: When the CPU, the graphics card or the memory goes above a % (or below it) for a while: a game or a render starts, a download finishes… «When it ends», when it's back to normal.
event.hint.load: It's measured every 2 s, as in Task Manager (GPU = its 3D engine). Examples: GPU above 50 % for 30 s → High performance plan, and «When it ends» → Balanced; CPU below 10 % for 600 s → shut down when a render finishes.
event.kind.AudioDevice.desc: When headphones, a USB or Bluetooth speaker… are connected, or one becomes the default output; «When it ends», when it is disconnected or stops being it.
event.summary.audioAny: When an audio device is connected
event.summary.audioDefaultAny: When the default audio output changes
event.hint.audio: Output devices (those in Windows Sound). The name can be a part: «JBL», «Headphones».
event.hint.network: The name is the one Windows gives the network: the Wi-Fi’s, or «Network 2» for a cable. The list shows the ones connected now.
event.hint.drive: A letter only matches that letter; a name is looked for in the drive’s label (the one shown in Explorer).
event.hint.file: Filter with wildcards: *.png, render_*.mp4… (* = any). It waits until the file stops growing for a second; each file fires the event once.
event.summary.power.Mains: When it goes back on mains
enum.powerSource.Mains: When it goes back on mains
event.hint.power: Only on computers with a battery (or a UPS that tells Windows).

kboard.createCommand: Create a command that switches this profile on and off

kboard.captureSourceHint: Press the key, button or combination you want to remap
kboard.surfaceHint: Click a key or button to choose what it does. Remapped keys light up and show their new function.
kboard.surfaceDotHint: The dot means the key has remaps with other modifiers.
kboard.keysHint: The key stays down while you hold the original one: it works for modifiers (Caps Lock → Ctrl) and in games.
kboard.textHint: Typed as is, with any keyboard layout. Line breaks press Enter.
kboard.commandHint: Runs the command when the key is pressed; the key no longer reaches the application.
kboard.disableHint: The key or button does nothing while the profile is on.
kboard.normalHint: The key works normally. Choose another option to remap it.
kboard.warnClick: Careful: this profile works in every application. Changing the left or right click affects everything, K-Desktop included. If something goes wrong, switch the profile off from the tray icon.
kboard.warnSame: The key is remapped to itself: nothing changes.
kboard.noRemaps: This profile does not change any key yet.

tips.title: Did you know…?
tip.w.desktop: Shows the desktop at once; press it again to bring the windows back.
tip.w.lock: Locks the PC when you step away; everything stays open as you left it.
tip.w.run: Opens the Run box: type cmd, regedit, control, %temp%…
tip.w.search: Searches apps, files and settings. Pressing Win and just typing works too.
tip.w.quicklink: Opens the quick link menu: Task Manager, Terminal, Disk Management, shut down…
tip.w.clipboard: Clipboard history: paste anything you copied earlier, not just the last thing.
tip.w.emoji: Emoji, symbol (≠ € ©…) and GIF panel in any text box.
tip.w.snip: Snips part of the screen and copies it to the clipboard.
tip.w.printscreen: Captures the whole screen and saves it in Pictures\Screenshots.
tip.w.taskview: Task view: every window and the virtual desktops.
tip.w.newdesktop: Creates a new virtual desktop and switches to it.
tip.w.switchdesktop: Switches to the previous or next virtual desktop.
tip.w.closedesktop: Closes the current virtual desktop (its windows move to the next one).
tip.w.snaplayouts: Shows the snap layouts to place the window in a grid.
tip.w.minimize: Restores a maximized window; press it again to minimize it.
tip.w.snapside: Snaps the window to the left or right half of the screen.
tip.w.monitor: Moves the window to the other screen.
tip.w.stretch: Stretches the window to the full height of the screen, keeping its width.
tip.w.shake: Minimizes everything but the active window; repeat to bring them back.
tip.w.taskbarN: Opens the app pinned at that position of the taskbar, or switches to it.
tip.w.taskbarNew: Opens another window of the app pinned at that position.
tip.w.taskbarAdmin: Opens the app pinned at that position as administrator.
tip.w.taskbarCycle: Goes through the taskbar icons with the arrows; Enter opens.
tip.w.tray: Moves the focus to the notification area (tray icons).
tip.w.notifications: Opens the notifications and the calendar.
tip.w.quicksettings: Quick settings: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, volume, brightness, airplane mode…
tip.w.project: Chooses how to use several screens: duplicate, extend or just one.
tip.w.cast: Connects to a wireless display or device.
tip.w.gamebar: Game Bar: recording, screenshots, performance and audio.
tip.w.record: Starts or stops recording the active window (Game Bar).
tip.w.dictation: Voice typing in any text box.
tip.w.language: Switches the input language or keyboard layout.
tip.w.magnifier: Magnifier: zooms the screen in and out. Win + Esc closes it.
tip.w.peek: Peeks at the desktop while you hold it.
tip.w.secure: Security screen: lock, switch user, sign out or Task Manager.
tip.w.alttab: Switches windows. With Ctrl the switcher stays open and you pick with the arrows.
tip.w.altf4: Closes the active window. On the desktop, opens the shut down dialog.
tip.w.graphics: Restarts the graphics driver: handy when the screen goes black or freezes.
tip.w.hdr: Turns HDR on or off on displays that support it.
tip.w.mute: Mutes or unmutes the microphone in supported calls.
tip.e.address: Jumps to the address bar to type a path (or cmd to open a console there).
tip.e.newwindow: Opens another window on the same folder.
tip.e.newtab: Opens a new tab in File Explorer.
tip.e.closetab: Closes the tab or the window.
tip.e.switchtab: Goes to the next or previous tab.
tip.e.rename: Renames the item; Tab moves on to rename the next one.
tip.e.properties: Opens the properties of the selected item.
tip.e.preview: Shows or hides the preview pane.
tip.e.details: Shows or hides the details pane.
tip.e.up: Goes up to the parent folder.
tip.e.back: Goes back to the previous folder or forward again.
tip.e.copypath: Copies the full path of the selected file.
tip.e.permanent: Deletes without using the Recycle Bin (careful!).
tip.e.views: Changes the view: large icons, list, details, tiles…
tip.e.zoom: Changes the icon size without any menu.
tip.e.morecontext: Opens the full classic context menu, with extras like “Copy as path”.
tip.e.expand: In the folder tree: expands every subfolder of the selected one.
tip.e.fullscreen: Makes the File Explorer window full screen.
tip.e.taskbarShift: On the taskbar: opens another window of that app.
tip.e.taskbarAdmin: On the taskbar: opens the app as administrator.
tip.e.taskbarMiddle: On the taskbar: opens another window of that app.
tip.e.taskbarCtrl: On the taskbar: cycles through the windows of the app one by one.
tip.b.reopen: Reopens the last closed tab (repeat to get more back).
tip.b.private.keys: Ctrl + Shift + N | Ctrl + Shift + P
tip.b.private: Private / incognito window (Chrome and Edge · Firefox).
tip.b.tabnum: Jumps to the tab at that position.
tip.b.address: Selects the address bar to type another address or search.
tip.b.addressnewtab: In the address bar: opens the address in a new tab.
tip.b.dotcom: In the address bar: adds www. and .com to what you typed.
tip.b.find: Finds in the page; F3 / Shift + F3 go to the next or previous match.
tip.b.hardrefresh: Reloads the page bypassing the cache.
tip.b.back: Previous or next page (same as Mouse 4 and Mouse 5).
tip.b.bookmarksbar: Shows or hides the bookmarks bar.
tip.b.print: Prints the page or saves it as PDF.
tip.b.zoom.keys: Ctrl + Wheel | Ctrl + Plus | Ctrl + Minus
tip.b.zoom: Zooms the page in or out.
tip.b.space: Scrolls down or up one screen.
tip.b.topbottom: Goes to the top or bottom of the page.
tip.b.middleclick: On a link, opens it in the background; on a tab, closes it.
tip.b.ctrlclick: Opens the link in a background tab.
tip.b.ctrlshiftclick: Opens the link in a tab and jumps to it.
tip.b.shiftclick: Opens the link in a new window.
tip.b.alttext: Selects the text of a link without opening it.
tip.b.taskmgr: Browser task manager: which tab uses the most (Chrome and Edge).
tip.t.word: Moves the cursor word by word.
tip.t.delword: Deletes the previous or next word in one go.
tip.t.line: Goes to the start or end of the line.
tip.t.selline: Selects to the start or end of the line.
tip.t.doc: Goes to the start or end of the document.
tip.t.undo: Undo or redo (in File Explorer too: undoes moving, copying or deleting files).
tip.t.clipboard.keys: Ctrl + C | Ctrl + X | Ctrl + V
tip.t.insert: Copy and paste with the classic keys (works in consoles and terminals).
tip.t.clicks: Selects the whole word or paragraph.
tip.t.paragraph: Jumps to the previous or next paragraph.
tip.t.altcode: With the numeric keypad, types characters by their code: © (0169), € (0128), ñ (0241)…
tip.k.qmleft: In the QuickMenu, runs the item and closes the menu.
tip.k.qmright: In the QuickMenu, runs the item and keeps the menu open to launch several.
tip.k.qmmiddle: In the QuickMenu, opens K-Desktop to edit the command, or the whole menu.
tip.k.qmkeys: The QuickMenu works with the keyboard; first letters jump to each item and Shift + Enter keeps it open.
tip.k.qmtoggle: Pressing the QuickMenu hotkey again closes it.
tip.k.esc: Cancels K-Desktop countdowns: shutdowns, waits and messages.
tip.k.shiftesc: Stops the macro being played and releases any keys it was holding.
tip.k.show.keys: Ctrl + Alt + Home | Ctrl + Alt + End
tip.k.show: Opens or exits K-Desktop (changeable in Settings).
tip.k.chord: Combining mouse buttons (a side button plus another button or the wheel) gives lots of extra shortcuts without the keyboard.
tip.k.kboard: With K-Board you can turn Caps Lock into Ctrl, disable the Windows key in games or make a side button copy and paste.

assistant.prompt.tools: Use a tool when the user asks you to do something or to know something it knows (the time, their notes, their timers, a calculation): don't guess. Their K-Desktop commands run with run_command; if they ask what a command does or which commands they have, look it up with describe_command or find_command: don't make up what they do.

assistant.prompt.memory: What you know about the user (use it only when it fits, don't recite it):
assistant.memory.learn:
You read an exchange between a user and their assistant. Extract ONLY new, lasting facts about the user worth remembering for months: their name, family, pets, work or studies, likes and hobbies, health, important dates and plans. Only take what the user says about themselves, never what the assistant says.
Don't include greetings, passing moods, questions, one-off requests or anything about the assistant. Don't repeat what is already known.
Write each fact in English, as a short sentence in the third person ("Their name is Mark", "They love coffee").
Reply ONLY with JSON: {"memories":[{"text":"...","kind":"fact|like|event","importance":0.0-1.0}]}
If there is nothing new, reply {"memories":[]}.
